_about: EXAMPLE QUESTIONS — the questions a first-time reader is offered, per machine, per language.
RULED BY ADR-011. This file is CANONICAL FOR WHAT A USER IS OFFERED, and editing it is a
canonical for retrieval MEASUREMENT (ADR-008) and editing that one is a measurement change.
The two overlap and will drift, which is correct: the measurement set must keep its Mode B
cases and this set must never have any.
EVERY QUESTION HERE MUST YIELD MODE A. An example that lands on the ungrounded card teaches the
opposite of the lesson it exists for. Each carries the `source` protocol id it was written
against, so ExampleQuestionsTest fails when that protocol leaves the corpus rather than the
demo failing in front of a reader.
WHY MOST OF THEM CARRY AN ERROR CODE, and it is not decoration: a code is a code-like term, so
ADR-009's exact-term clause grounds the answer even when the cosine score alone would not.
